record.original_question: Given a pattern p and an integer n, what is the complexity of deciding whether the recursively defined word Z_n encounters p in the abelian sense?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define the Zimin words over an infinite alphabet of variables x_1, x_2, ... recursively by Z_1 = x_1 and Z_{k+1} = Z_k x_{k+1} Z_k for k >= 1. A pattern is a nonempty word p = p_1 p_2 ... p_m over a finite set of variables. For a finite word w over some alphabet Σ, write |w|_a for the number of occurrences of letter a in w, and call two words u, v abelian-equivalent (u ~_ab v) if they have the same length and |u|_a = |v|_a for every letter a.

Say that a word w encounters the pattern p in the abelian sense if w has a factor of the form w = u · f(p_1) f(p_2) ... f(p_m) · v, where f is a map sending each variable of p to a nonempty word over Σ, such that whenever p_i and p_j denote the same variable, the words f(p_i) and f(p_j) are abelian-equivalent (in particular have the same length).

Question: Determine the computational complexity of the following decision problem. Given as input a pattern p (encoded as a word over a variable alphabet) and a positive integer n (encoded in unary or binary), decide whether the Zimin word Z_n encounters p in the abelian sense.
artifact.category_tag: combinatorics on words / abelian pattern avoidance
artifact.status_search_result: The exact computational complexity of deciding whether the Zimin word Z_n encounters a given pattern p in the abelian sense is not pinned down in the literature. Related work establishes a doubly-exponential upper bound for encountering Zimin patterns in the abelian sense and decidability results for unavoidability, but no precise complexity classification (e.g. matching upper and lower bounds) for this specific decision problem has been reported, so the question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On Long Words Avoiding Zimin Patterns
status_evidence.snippet: Tower-of-exponential bounds for encountering Zimin patterns; abelian variant has doubly-exponential bound.
status_evidence.claim: Bounds are known for Zimin pattern encountering, including an abelian variant, but a precise complexity for deciding abelian encounter by Z_n is not given.

status_evidence.title: Avoiding Patterns in the Abelian Sense
status_evidence.snippet: Studies abelian avoidance of patterns; foundational results on which patterns are abelian-avoidable.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational paper on abelian pattern avoidance; does not resolve the decision complexity of abelian encounter in Zimin words.

status_evidence.title: Abelian combinatorics on words: A survey
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of abelian combinatorics on words listing open problems.
status_evidence.claim: Recent survey lists abelian pattern problems among ongoing research, with no definitive complexity classification cited for this question.
